title: Compact timeline: ratio-driven zoom accessibility and locale-aware unit abbreviations — prototype review
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background:
We have multiple compact timeline widgets used across Cost Explorer and Route Rollouts where dense data + small visual footprint causes accessibility regressions under text-scaling, high-contrast themes, and localized number formats. This ticket documents a prototype and design review for two coupled features: 1) ratio-driven zoom behavior for compact timelines to preserve visual proportions when users increase text size or use assistive magnifiers, and 2) locale-aware unit abbreviations (compact number format) with accessible tooltips and expansion controls for screen readers and keyboard users.

Goals:
- Provide a deterministic zoom model that scales timelines by a content ratio rather than absolute px, preserving hit targets and layout flow under 125%–300% text scaling and browser zoom.
- Ensure keyboard-focus order and visible focus rings remain stable when the timeline reflows from zoom changes.
- Replace hard-coded "K/M" suffixes with Intl.NumberFormat(compact) where available, and provide explicit aria-labels and on-focus expansion for locales that require different short-scale words (eg. "1 Mio" vs "1M").
- Maintain color contrast for timeline strokes and small labels in both default and high-contrast modes, using a variable token mapping and a fallback outline for low-contrast cases.
- Provide an accessible toggle for expanding compact labels to full numbers for users who need explicit values.

Prototype and artifacts:
- Figma prototype (interactive states): https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/compact-timeline-zoom-proto
- Confluence PRD + accessibility checklist: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/UX/Compact+Timeline+Zoom+and+Locale+Abbrev+PRD
- Clickthrough prototype (VoiceOver / NVDA scenarios): https://redwood-internal.github.io/prototypes/compact-timeline-2026-03
- Initial engineering spike: GH PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4567

Design decisions made in prototype:
- Zoom model: compute a timelineScale value = clamp(1, userFontScale * contentRatio, 3). contentRatio is derived from the visible density (events per px) so dense timelines compress visually but preserve label legibility by increasing vertical spacing slightly.
- Units: use Intl.NumberFormat(locale, { notation: 'compact', compactDisplay: 'short' }) as primary. For locales lacking compact formatting or where ambiguity exists, show compact form plus visually-hidden full number via aria-label and a small "expand" affordance on focus (keyboard: Enter toggles expansion).
- Focus management: add focus sentinels at timeline container start/end and ensure arrow-key left/right moves between event chips. Focus ring uses token --focus-outline which adapts in high-contrast mode to a 3:1 border + 4:1 inner glow to meet WCAG for small targets.
- Color tokens: timeline stroke uses semantic token --timeline-stroke; when contrast < 4.5:1, an outline is drawn using --timeline-contrast-fallback. We also include a dashed pattern overlay as a non-color redundant indicator when requested via OS high-contrast.

Acceptance criteria:
- Keyboard navigation: Tab lands on the timeline container, then arrow keys navigate event chips; screen reader announces chip label and full numeric value when expansion is toggled.
- Scaling: At 150% and 200% text scaling in Chrome/Firefox/Safari, timeline layout remains usable and hit targets are >= 24px recommended.
- Contrast: All labels and strokes pass 4.5:1 for body text and 3:1 for larger labels in default theme; high-contrast toggle demonstrates redundant indicators.
- i18n: For en, fr, ja, ar locales confirm compact notation renders appropriate short-forms and aria-labels present full numeric strings.
- Performance: Rendering change under scale must not exceed 30ms for typical timelines (<= 200 events).

Notes on trade-offs and open questions:
- Using compact notation improves density but can conceal magnitude for some locales. The expansion affordance addresses this but adds interaction cost. Need PM alignment on default expanded/compact setting per user preferences.
- The ratio-driven zoom improves perceived consistency but may shift layout flow for other dashboard components; engineering will gate with an opt-in toggle behind feature flag for rollout.
- Screen magnifier testing uncovered that browser zoom + OS magnifier produce different reflow patterns; QA matrix must include real device/manual tests (not just browser devtools).

Next steps and owner tasks:
- Design: finalize tokens and microcopy for expand affordance (Maya) — due 2026-03-08.
- Eng: spike to implement Intl fallback and feature flag for scale model (Liam) — PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4567.
- A11y: run NVDA/VoiceOver scripts with locales and report failures back into this ticket (Accessibility team contact: Priya Patel).
- QA: create automated visual tests at 100%, 150%, 200% scales and add to Percy set.

Estimated rollout plan:
1) Behind feature flag for internal canary users (console-2026.04-alpha).
2) Collect behavioral metrics (focus events, expand toggles, error rates) for two weeks.
3) Gradual rollout to 10% then 50% while monitoring keyboard and screen reader errors.

Deliverables in this ticket:
- Finalized Figma screens with annotated A11y steps.
- Engineering spike PR with prototype implementation and feature flag.
- Accessibility test matrix and QA runbook.
comments: 2026-03-02 Maya Chen: Uploaded revised Figma with high-contrast overlay spec and added explicit aria-label examples for Japanese number formatting.

2026-03-04 Priya Patel (A11y): Ran initial NVDA pass. Two issues: 1) compact abbreviations announced as literal letters "K" instead of expanded number in en-GB with TalkBack; 2) focus order resets after zoom change in Firefox. Added repro steps in a11y doc.

2026-03-05 Maya Chen: Updated spec to include aria-live polite region for expansion toggles and clarified keyboard interactions (Enter to expand, Escape to collapse). Added fallback microcopy for locales without compact notation.

2026-03-07 Liam O'Connor: Addressed NVDA issue by shipping aria-label fallback in spike. Firefox focus reset investigated — likely due to forced DOM reflow; experimenting with transform-based scale to avoid re-rendering children.

2026-03-09 QA Team: Visual tests added to Percy for 100/150/200% scales. Two visual diffs flagged for tiny label clipping at 200% in compact mode. Linked screenshots: https://percy.io/redwood/compact-timeline/diffs.
2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Requested design review with PM and Eng. Scheduled sync 2026-03-12 to approve rollout gating and default preference behavior.
